commits.message:
feat(daemon): the host holds a renderer's stored state under its profile, and the renderer is built from it (uh4)

The host keeps every store a renderer reads (session picks and drafts,
settings history, the doctor's documents) in memory under the profile the
renderer's name derives, writes each file behind it, and flushes them at its
close. A renderer is constructed from what the host holds then, and changes
it only by the store writes each turn returns, so restarting the renderer
process keeps every pick, draft and undo step. A renderer under a second
name reads and writes only its own profile's files.

The host keeps a book of each session's durable context (its config origin
and Claude Code's directory) from its newest request, in its own state
directory. A click carries its session's context: live when the session has
been heard since the daemon started, else read back from the book with no
live part. What a client reports now (its tmux pane, terminal and env) is
never kept, so after a restart a slash click is refused and a lane setup
owed until the session's next request. The renderer no longer records an
origin or hints in session state.

Undo steps name a layer by its role and a digest of its file, never a path.
A breach's renderer heap snapshot streams over the renderer's lines and the
host writes it, so the renderer process opens no file.

fix(test): the request-limits config stops being a fifo before its hold ends (6sc)

On macOS the config watch heard the test's write to the fifo and re-read the path after the writer closed, blocking the daemon's loop for good. A plain file is renamed over the fifo while the render's read still holds the loop, so the render reads on through its open descriptor and every later open of the path gets a plain file.

chore(release): set `package.json` to 1.229.0
